newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer says opens drugs plant in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Bayer says opens drugs plant in Pakistan.

text.p: German chemicals group Bayer AG said on Friday that it had opened a pharmaceuticals plant in Pakistan for the manufacture of tablets and cream-based medical treatments.
Bayer said the new plant had meant an investment of 230 million rupees or around $6.0 million.

"We have great confidence in the future development of Pakistan's business environment and see especially good perspectives for the health care sector," Clemens Kaiser, head of Bayer pharmaceuticals in Asia, Africa, South America and eastern Europe, said in a statement.
Products to be manufactured at the plant include Ciprobay, an antibiotic, Resochin, a treatment for malaria, the anti-diabetic drug Glucobay and the Canesten anti-fungal treatment, Bayer said.
